items.title: A weakly etale algebra over a field is reduced, integral, a filtered colimit of finite separable products, and closed under subalgebras, quotients and tensor products
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six structural properties of a K-algebra B that is weakly etale over a field K: that B is reduced; that B is integral over K; that every finitely generated K-subalgebra of B is a finite product of finite separable extensions of K; that B is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents, in which case it is a separable algebraic extension of K; that every subalgebra or quotient algebra of B is again weakly etale over K; and that the tensor product of two such algebras is again weakly etale (source lines 30845-30859). The proof assembles these from the two preceding results and from the structure of etale algebras over a field. Part (1) is drawn from the absolutely-flat-over-absolutely-flat lemma. Part (3) follows from the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma together with the fact that etale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (proof lines 30861-30867). Part (3) implies (2), and part (4) follows from (3) because a product of fields is a field exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents (proof lines 30868-30870). The substantive part is (5): for a subalgebra S of B the proof observes that S is the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, each of which is etale over K by the above, and hence S is weakly etale by the absolutely-flat-over-field lemma; for a quotient B -> Q the proof uses that Q is the filtered colimit of quotients of finite products of finite separable extensions, and that any quotient of such a product is itself a sub-product, so the result follows by the same reasoning (proof lines 30873-30883). Part (6) is then obtained either similarly or by combining the base change and composition permanence lemmas (proof lines 30886-30888). The non-routine content is the filtered-colimit argument for subalgebras and the sub-product description of quotients of finite separable products.
